extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students and researchers in complex analysis, elliptic functions, and modular forms
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of the Weierstrass ℘-function, Eisenstein series, and Jacobi theta function: definitions, convergence criteria, key properties (periodicity, parity, poles/zeros), series/product expansions, and modular transformation laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.5 — convergence of two lattice series (r > 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two series Σ_{(n,m)≠(0,0)} 1/(|n|+|m|)^r and Σ_{n+mτ ∈ Λ*} 1/|n + mτ|^r converge if r > 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: sum first in m then in n and apply integral comparison; use comparison inequalities reducing to a 1/|n|^{r−1} tail. For the second series, reduce to showing |n|+|m| ≤ c|n + τ m| for τ in the upper half-plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate — equivalence |n|+|m| ≈ |n + mτ| for τ ∈ H
rubrics_metrics.description: For τ = s + it with t > 0, one has |n + mτ| = [(n + ms)^2 + (mt)^2]^{1/2} ≈ |n + ms| + |mt| ≈ |n| + |m|; hence |n|+|m| (cid:1) |n+mτ| and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce absolute convergence results uniformly in Im(τ) ≥ δ > 0 and to compare growth of lattice points; consider separate cases |n| ≤ 2|m||s| and |n| ≥ 2|m||s|.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform convergence remark for lattice power series (r>2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When r > 2 the series Σ_{n+mτ ∈ Λ*} |n + mτ|^{-r} converges uniformly in every half-plane Im(τ) ≥ δ > 0. In contrast, the series fails to converge when r = 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical uniformity underpins holomorphy in τ for Eisenstein series and related objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Weierstrass ℘-function (regularized series)
rubrics_metrics.description: ℘(z) = 1/z^2 + Σ_{ω∈Λ*} (1/(z+ω)^2 − 1/ω^2), where Λ is the lattice and Λ* = Λ \ {(0,0)}. The subtraction of 1/ω^2 makes the sum converge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bracketed term is O(1/|ω|^3) as |ω|→∞, so the tail defines a holomorphic function on bounded discs; the finite part exhibits the double poles.

rubrics_metrics.name: ℘ is meromorphic with double poles at lattice points
rubrics_metrics.description: The series for ℘ defines a meromorphic function having double poles exactly at the lattice points of Λ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split the defining sum into |ω| ≤ 2R (finite sum giving poles in |z|<R) and |ω|>2R (tail O(1/|ω|^3) giving holomorphic contribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.6 — ℘ is elliptic of order 2 with periods 1 and τ
rubrics_metrics.description: The function ℘ is an elliptic function that has periods 1 and τ, and double poles at the lattice points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate the defining series termwise: ℘'(z) = −2 Σ 1/(z + n + mτ)^3 converges absolutely for z not a lattice point (case r=3 of Lemma 1.5). Differentiation removes the subtraction term and shows ℘' is periodic, hence ℘ is periodic up to constants; parity arguments (℘ even) force those constants to vanish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity: ℘ even and ℘' odd; vanishing of ℘' at half-periods
rubrics_metrics.description: ℘(−z) = ℘(z) (℘ is even), so ℘' is odd. Consequently ℘'(1/2) = ℘'(τ/2) = ℘'((1+τ)/2) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evenness follows from grouping ω with −ω in the lattice sum; the half-period points are roots of ℘' inside the fundamental parallelogram and have multiplicity 1 for ℘' and multiplicity 2 for the corresponding level sets of ℘.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.7 — cubic relation for (℘')^2
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows by comparing zeros and poles: both sides have double zeros at half-periods and poles of order 6 at lattice points, so their quotient is a doubly-periodic holomorphic function hence constant; matching Laurent leading terms near 0 gives constant = 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality: every elliptic function rational in ℘ and ℘'
rubrics_metrics.description: Every elliptic function f with periods 1 and τ is a rational function of ℘ and ℘'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 1.9: every even elliptic function is a rational function of ℘. Decompose general f into even + odd parts: feven is rational in ℘, and fodd/℘' is even so rational in ℘; hence f is rational in ℘ and ℘'. Construction uses products of factors ℘(z) − ℘(a_j) to match zeros/poles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Eisenstein series Ek(τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ek(τ) = Σ_{(n,m)≠(0,0)} 1/(n + mτ)^k for integer k ≥ 3 and τ in the upper half-plane; equivalently Ek(τ) = Σ_{ω∈Λ*} 1/ω^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ek arises naturally from the lattice sums and connects to coefficients in ℘-expansion and modular behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.1 — basic properties of Eisenstein series
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Ek(τ) converges if k ≥ 3 and is holomorphic in the upper half-plane; (ii) Ek(τ) = 0 if k is odd; (iii) modular-type transformations: Ek(τ + 1) = Ek(τ) and Ek(τ) = τ^{−k} Ek(−1/τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convergence follows from Lemma 1.5 uniformly in Im(τ) ≥ δ; vanishing for odd k by symmetry (replace (n,m) by (−n,−m)); transformation laws via rearrangement and substitution in the double sum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.2 — Laurent expansion of ℘ near 0
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand 1/(z−ω)^2 in powers of z/ω using the identity 1/(1−w)^2 = Σ (k+1) w^k and sum over the lattice to identify coefficients with Eisenstein series. Only even powers appear because of symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 2.3 — Weierstrass cubic in terms of Eisenstein series
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates Theorem 1.7 in terms of Eisenstein series; obtain by comparing series coefficients of ℘ and ℘' near 0 and using periodicity to conclude the difference is constant and equals zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.4 — Poisson-summation identity for 1/(n+τ)^k
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivable by Poisson summation applied to f(z) = 1/(z + τ)^k or by proving the k=2 case from cotangent formulas and differentiating repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.5 — Fourier expansion of Ek for even k ≥ 4
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: separate the n=0 contributions to identify 2ζ(k), then apply Lemma 2.4 (with τ replaced by mτ) and reorganize sums to express remaining part as the Fourier series with divisor-sum coefficients; check absolute convergence on Im(τ) ≥ t0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbidden Eisenstein series (k=2) and iterated-sum F(τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define F(τ) = Σ_{m} Σ_{n} 1/(n + mτ)^2 with summation in the indicated order (sum in n for fixed m then in m). This double sum converges in that order and equals F(τ) = 2 ζ(2) − 8 π^2 Σ_{r=1}^∞ σ(r) e^{2π i r τ}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the r=2 lattice series is not absolutely convergent, the iterated sum (summed in the specified order) converges and yields the stated Fourier expansion. Note F does not satisfy the naive modular relation F(−1/τ) τ^{−2} = F(τ); reversing summation order gives a different value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Jacobi theta function Θ(z|τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Θ(z|τ) = Σ_{n=−∞}^∞ e^{π i n^2 τ} e^{2π i n z}, defined for z ∈ C and τ ∈ H. Specializations: θ(τ) = Θ(0|τ), ϑ(t) = θ(i t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Θ is central to the interplay between elliptic and modular aspects (period 1 and quasi-period τ in z; modular transformations in τ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.1 — structural properties of Θ
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Θ is entire in z and holomorphic in τ; (ii) Θ(z+1|τ) = Θ(z|τ); (iii) Θ(z+τ|τ) = Θ(z|τ) e^{−π i τ} e^{−2π i z}; (iv) Θ(z|τ) = 0 whenever z = 1/2 + τ/2 + n + mτ (n,m∈Z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convergence justification uses bounds on |q| = |e^{π i τ}| and uniform convergence on bounded z for Im(τ) bounded below; (iv) shown by pairing indices n and −n−1 to cancel terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple-product Π(z|τ) and its properties (Proposition 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Π(z|τ) = Π_{n=1}^∞ (1 − q^{2n})(1 + q^{2n−1} e^{2π i z})(1 + q^{2n−1} e^{−2π i z}), with q = e^{π i τ}. Π(z|τ) is entire in z, holomorphic in τ, periodic in z with period 1, satisfies Π(z+τ|τ) = Π(z|τ) e^{−π i τ} e^{−2π i z}, and has simple zeros exactly at z = 1/2 + τ/2 + n + mτ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zeros come from vanishing of the second/third factors when q^{2n−1} e^{±2π i z} = −1; simplicity follows because factors vanish to first order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.3 — product formula Θ = Π
rubrics_metrics.description: For all z ∈ C and τ ∈ H, Θ(z|τ) = Π(z|τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: consider quotient F(z)=Θ/Π which is entire and doubly-periodic hence constant; evaluate special z-values (e.g., z=1/2 and z=1/4) to show the constant equals 1 using q→0 limits (iterate τ→4τ scaling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 1.5 — (log Θ)'' is an elliptic function of order 2
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed τ ∈ H, the function (log Θ(z|τ))'' = Θ Θ'''' − (Θ'')^2 over Θ^2 (primes are derivatives in z) is an elliptic function of order 2 with periods 1 and τ and with a double pole at z = 1/2 + τ/2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate the periodicity/quasi-periodicity relations for Θ to see that (log Θ)'' is doubly-periodic; the unique zero of Θ in the fundamental parallelogram implies the pole structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.6 — modular transformation of Θ under τ → −1/τ
rubrics_metrics.description: For τ ∈ H and all z ∈ C, Θ(z| −1/τ) = (τ / i)^{1/2} e^{π i τ z^2} Θ(z τ | τ). (Here τ / i denotes the branch of the square root positive on the positive imaginary axis.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to the Poisson summation identity for Gaussian sums; check real z and τ = i t > 0 and extend by analyticity in z and τ. Specializing z=0 yields θ(−1/τ) = (τ / i)^{1/2} θ(τ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 1.7 — theta modular relation at z=0
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from Theorem 1.6 by setting z=0; matches the classical functional equation for the theta null.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedekind eta function and its modular transformation (Proposition 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive from differentiating the theta transformation law at the zero z0 = 1/2 + τ/2 and evaluating products/factors; choose cube roots consistently using positivity on the imaginary axis and analytic continuation.
